title: Detach can race Codex thread-setup completion (reverse thread map inserted after the session lock is released)
outcome:
Found by the Codex reviewer during round-2 review of the thread-setup state machine. PRE-EXISTING (predates the parking work) but adjacent to it.

complete_shared_codex_thread_setup (codex.rs) releases the sessions lock before inserting the reverse thread_id -> session_id mapping into thread_sessions. session_runtime.rs detach can run between those two operations: it misses the not-yet-inserted mapping, so completion then inserts a stale mapping and queues a turn AFTER the session was detached.

Fix direction: hold the sessions lock through reverse-map registration, or re-validate that the session is still attached immediately before the StartTurnAfterSetup handoff.
acceptance: A deterministic regression interleaves detach with thread-setup completion at the forward/reverse registration boundary and proves a detached attachment leaves neither mapping nor a usable StartTurnAfterSetup handoff.
Current attached setup completion still binds both maps and returns its parked command exactly once; stale setup completion cannot overwrite a successor attachment.
The change preserves the existing shared-Codex lock order and process/session ownership, with no new parallel registry.
The final input passes focused compile/tests covering the race and existing setup/detach controls, the independent review pair, and the integration owner's exact-input full gate.
